notes.text: Typescript letter-like sheet headed VII 2, with an upper-left SGA 4 XVI reference, handwritten corrections and marginal marks. No salutation, signature or date is present. The pencilled archive number 29 is retained only in a comment. H has a textual witness for page 29 and explicitly excludes machine x cancellations from its scope.
notes.basis: All three complete page readings and inventories; main top-reference crop.

notes.text: The first paragraph says that 2.1.1 reduces to affine X, calls affine X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and relates the assertion to a base-change theorem and reductions through 2.1.5 and transcendence degree one. These reductions and the cited numbered theorem are reported as source assertions. Their complete statements are absent from this sheet, so they have not been verified here.
notes.basis: Unanimous first-paragraph wording, with local ink adjudications for the reference and insertion.

notes.text: The phrase et qui est essentiellement is an unfinished typed insertion and is not completed. The corps de call points before base in the later base-change phrase. The source says s’il ne l’est déjà and je n’ai pas les textes en main, expressly recording the writer’s uncertainty about whether 2.1.1 was already stated. It proposes a future presentation in a re-edition; the note does not establish what any edition eventually contained.
notes.basis: All three readings, prior C questions, and main corps de crop; documentary observation.

notes.text: The second paragraph proposes grouping 2.1.1 and 2.1.7 and treating 2.1.5 as a corollary. The following instruction and proposed pro-lisse/lisse replacement by an asphericity condition are cancelled within a stepped, obliquely crossed graphic. Their cancellation is preserved without inferring whether they were rejected mathematically or merely rewritten. The terminal example period lies outside the visible cancellation.
notes.basis: Main cancellation crop and all three full readings.

notes.text: The literal tH., 2.12 and il sont are retained. The initial dash and the semicolon after définitions are resolved from their separate strokes, while the stop after rappels and the raised 1-/l- remain uncertain. Main preserves three separate underlines and the two fine local pen traces rather than merging them with the cancellation outline.
notes.basis: Main cancellation and énoncés crops; explicit outcomes for prior C questions.

notes.text: The marginal note remains partly uncertain: si on utilise is tentative, a separate un/en/on follows, ailleurs is resolved, and only the clipped initial c of canonique is marked. Its quotes, final comma and diagonal left placement are retained. The lower reference has barred IV and an inserted barred V; its crossed typed numeral is resolved as 5. The cancelled final line ends with d and is not completed.

notes.text: The first SGA reference has V/4 overprint components with unresolved strike order. The envers initial may be repeated e or an E/e correction in either order. A small comma-shaped mark after the second th. is retained uncertainly, and the detached lower mark is drawn as five near-vertical segments without textual interpretation.
notes.basis: Main enlarged overprint, punctuation and lower-stroke crops; these are ink decisions, not mathematical corrections.

notes.text: A targeted check confirms the limited implication used in the opening: an affine scheme X=Spec A is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Refining an open cover by principal opens gives elements generating the unit ideal, and a finite expression for 1 supplies a finite subcover. The absolute diagonal is induced by the surjective multiplication A tensor_Z A to A, hence is a closed immersion and quasi-compact. This checks only that implication, not any numbered reduction or base-change theorem in the letter.
notes.basis: Actual main-reader argument in decisions/scan030_math_work.md, connected to the unanimous observed opening sentence.
notes.event_outcome: Passed for affine X: finite principal-open subcover and closed absolute diagonal establish quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. No other source theorem or reduction checked.

notes.text: The principal-open basis, existence of maximal ideals above proper ideals, affine product and closed-immersion descriptions, and the diagonal criterion for quasi-separatedness are standard background used in the targeted argument. They were not independently reproved in this run.
notes.event_type: carried as background without fault found
notes.event_outcome: These standard algebraic-geometric facts are background assumptions for the limited affine implication; no independent proof of those foundations claimed.
